schema.description: One workout logged in the Strong app, shaped as an IEEE 1752 physical-activity-1.0 payload as strength_training, with the workout's sets beside it. The extractor records/extract/strong_csv.py in anam-importers writes a records file from a Strong CSV export, one record per workout, and the records importer sends it. Values are Strong's own, apart from the start time and the capped duration, which the extractor derives: Strong keeps a workout open until the next one starts, so the interval is at most 3 hours (duration_capped) and Strong's figure stays as reported_duration_sec. This is the Strong leaf of activity.exercise-session: Strong's own payload shape, named for its vendor, so a reader asks about exercise across the leaves by the prefix activity.exercise-session. and knows which shape each fact has. Version 1 is activity.exercise-session v2 cut to the fields Strong writes, each with the same rules, and its facets came across in the vendor-leaf rename (renames/vendor-leaves.json), each the next version of itself with its payload unchanged. The shared core, id, activity_name, effective_time_frame and source, is the same on all four leaves of activity.exercise-session (internal/def/shared-core.json). Version 2 requires source_time, every other rule unchanged.

activity_name.description: The IEEE 1752 activity name: strength_training for every Strong workout.

duration_capped.description: True when Strong's reported duration was zero or below, or over 3 hours, so the interval's duration was set to 3 hours by the extractor (Matt's rule). Absent otherwise.

effective_time_frame.description: When the session happened, as an IEEE 1752 time interval.

duration.description: The session's length in seconds: Strong's reported duration, or 3 hours when duration_capped.

value.description: Seconds, a whole or decimal number.

start_date_time.description: The start, ISO 8601 with offset, to the second, derived by the extractor: Strong's "Date" column read as Sydney time, so a workout logged abroad is placed as if at home. This is the fact time.

exercises.description: The workout's exercise names in the order Strong first lists them, from the "Exercise Name" column.

id.description: The records row's id: strong:session: and the workout's start as Strong's "Date" column writes it.

reported_duration_sec.description: Strong's "Duration (sec)" for the workout, always kept as reported, even when it is unusable.

sets.description: Every row of the Strong workout in file order, set by set, rest timers and notes included.

items.description: One Strong CSV row, minus the workout-level columns.

rpe.description: The "RPE" column, the rating of perceived exertion as logged.

seconds.description: The "Seconds" column, a timed set's length in seconds.

set.description: The "Set Order" column as text: a set number, or a marker such as "Rest Timer" or "Note" for rows that are not sets.

source.description: Which app the session came from: always "Strong", written by the extractor.

workout_notes.description: The workout's distinct "Workout Notes" values, sorted.

source_time.description: How Strong's clock was read: value is Strong's Date, the workout's start as a wall clock with no zone, read in the zone records/extract/strong_csv.py was given with --zone (basis configuration).

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.
